title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 125.9025: -(W + T) kernels, pass 2 by 128 and a 32-pair arrival loop at kappa = 1.0002

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack of proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^125.9025 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). It builds on this solver's 5f1ae3ce (125.9113; kappa = 1.0002 from the shipped hazard census, proof.md section 5.2, h = 0.000203 and p0 = 0.3902033, all unchanged) with three changes: kaankolcu's 4595bad7 kernels (pass 2 stores -(W + T), so y3' = lambda*(x3 - x_W) + y_W is a fused addition, and x3 subtracts a table field x_T + 2C0 with both borrow chains ending in ADC, so both folds are unsigned: 444 instructions per pass-2 walk); pass 2 unrolled 128 times, closed by SUBS and B.NE on a group counter in x18 (56,898 per 128 walks); and a straight-line arrival loop of 32 pairs whose parity paths rejoin at one BFI (31.015625 per arrival). The ordinary step is 99.515625 + 444.515625 + 31.015625 + 25391/2^20 = 575.0711 instructions; the declared run executes the shipped loops and arrival rows at exactly these counts. Rare exits charge 20 milli-units each and run the inline kernel's own instructions; the declared run enters all 1,167 exit stubs. Recovery probability is greater than 0.39000019 and therefore at least 0.39 (failure rows 1.0103e-7 < 1.1e-7). Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes; preprocessing is capped at 2^59 units, charged and included; nonuniform advice is zero. Exact ledger: S_ops = 1.0002*S0 = 2^126.7000183, phase 1 = 2^125.901830, hard extras = 2^112.575681, allowance = 2^114.3944, W_ledger = 2^125.9024664 < 2^125.9025; Markov ratio 0.000190100 (experiment.py's float ledger: 0.000190104) < 0.000203; certificate.py checks W^10000 < 1000^10000*2^1259025 and W^10000 > 1000^10000*2^1259024 exactly. No prior acceptance, review verdict or official score is a premise. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and the canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled toy pipeline of the checkpoint-only walk (even-y key, per-trail anchor phases) on subgroups of y^2=x^3+7, with node routing and a long-trail trap test; kernels: Python limb ports of the field kernels against big integers, and the shipped unrolled loops (with their rare exits, on constructed inputs that enter every stub), emitter wrappers and arrival rows executed by an AArch64 interpreter (kernels/a64.py) against affine secp256k1, a bit-exact model and the exact canonical rule, with instruction counts and the ledger of proof.md recomputed. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
